messages:
Maya (SRE): seeing a hard drop in eu-central-1 scheduler activity, control-plane heartbeats stopped ~10m ago. GPU node pool shows 0/120 ready. Anyone else seeing this?
IncidentBot: [ALERT] region: eu-central-1, severity: P1, rule: control-plane-heartbeat-missed, triggered at 2026-03-17T22:13:09Z.
Sam (Infra): confirmed — our monitoring shows the control-plane API is returning 502s and all health checks failing. Provider status page currently shows degraded network. Linking: https://status.cloudvendor.example.com/incidents/1234
Liam (Control Plane): logs look like the controller-manager lost connectivity to the etcd cluster. Lots of TLS handshake timeouts. Pushing a read-only request to etcd returns no leader.
Jules (Eng): what’s the blast radius? Are dedicated pools impacted or just hosted instances?
Maya (SRE): both dedicated and hosted in eu-central-1 are impacted. Autoscaler is reporting backoff when trying to provision new nodes: "rate limit exceeded" from provider API.
Sam (Infra): starting emergency traffic-shift to eu-west-1. Plan: 1) scale up eu-west-1 GPU pool by +30% from reserved, 2) shift 80% of user traffic via routing policy, 3) fallback to lightweight models if capacity short.
Maya (SRE): recommended commands in runbook:
```bash
# increase dedicated pool in eu-west-1
redwood infra scale --region eu-west-1 --pool gpu-reserved --delta +60
# shift traffic to eu-west-1
redwood route update --from-region eu-central-1 --to-region eu-west-1 --weight 80
```
Liam (Control Plane): doing staged route change now (canary 5% -> 20% -> 80%). Will monitor token latencies. If control-plane on eu-west spikes, we’ll abort.
Ana (Support): heads up — support page + status update draft ready. Recommending the message call out degraded API in eu-central-1 and that failover is in progress. I’ll post once we confirm the first shift step.
Sam (Infra): note: autoscale will trigger cloud burst and may incur spot/interruption risk. @finance FYI — short term spend will go up if we fully burst.
Jules (Eng): quick triage note: kernel logs from a few hosts show repeated NIC flapping at the hypervisor layer, plus provider BGP trace shows route instability. Could be provider network fabric issue rather than our control-plane code.
Maya (SRE): assigning on-call cloud escalation to Sam. Sam, please open a ticket with provider with packet captures and ask for fabric-level diag.
Sam (Infra): opened ticket #PV-7890 with provider and attached pcap + etcd leader logs. Provider escalated to network ops. ETA unknown.
Liam (Control Plane): continuing staged shift: canary 5% -> 20% completed, latencies normal for those requests. Proceeding to 80% now.
IncidentBot: [NOTE] automation-run: traffic-shift completed to 80% weight towards eu-west-1 at 2026-03-17T22:22:45Z.
Ana (Support): posted status update: "We’re experiencing degraded service in eu-central-1. Traffic is being shifted to eu-west-1; some requests may see higher latency. Engineers are investigating." :loud_sound:
Jules (Eng): can we enable auto-fallback to smaller models for non-critical routes? That reduces GPU footprint and helps capacity.
Maya (SRE): yes — enabling model fallback config for exploratory and background routes now. Command: `redwood config set fallback.models noncritical --active true`
Sam (Infra): provider just replied — they confirm fabric instability, working on route convergence, estimate 45-90 minutes. They recommend we keep failover in place.
Maya (SRE): status for page: keep message updated with ETA from provider and that failover is active. We’ll run a post-incident review after recovery.
Ana (Support): will add note about potential billing impact from burst.
Jules (Eng): logging note: saving current KV cache snapshots before full reroute to reduce cold-start cost when we flip back.
Maya (SRE): summary for ops channel: control-plane heartbeats died in eu-central-1 likely due to provider network fabric, we initiated traffic-shift to eu-west-1 and scaled capacity, provider engaged, on-call opened ticket #PV-7890. Next: monitor provider updates, reduce non-critical load, prepare rollback run if provider claims resolved.
Sam (Infra): ping if any spike > 2x baseline for latency/errors. I’ll keep provider channel open.
Liam (Control Plane): acknowledged, monitoring etcd leader election.
Ana (Support): updating customers now with current ETA window.
Maya (SRE): thanks all — collecting logs for postmortem. I’ll create the incident timeline once we stabilize. :white_check_mark:
